Dear Wanderer, as I write these words, I feel as though we are face to face.
Some time ago, this old man accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the local school. There, I saw the children sitting upright and engrossed in their books, so absorbed that they didn’t even notice our approach.
Curious, I wondered what marvelous texts could hold the attention of these usually restless youngsters. Upon asking, I learned that the books they were reading were gifts from you not long ago.
When I inquired further about what made these books so special, the children eagerly chimed in, and I realized you had thoughtfully chosen a different book for each child. Hearing that I was acquainted with you, they all begged me to convey their gratitude.
Yet, when pressed to express their thanks aloud, the little ones grew shy and tongue-tied. So, I suggested they put their thoughts into writing, and here they are, sealed within this letter—unread by me, I assure you!
Oh, and the children also entrusted me with a few drawings, inspired by the books you gave them. They insisted that you, of all people, would appreciate their masterpieces, for in their eyes, you have the finest taste.
Ha Ha, it seems that for any future tasks involving children, you are the one to turn to.
